title: Moments of random multiplicative functions with polynomial coefficients
summary: Let $f$ be a Steinhaus random multiplicative function and let $g$ be a polynomial of degree $d$. Write $S_N=N^{-1/2}\sum_{n\le N}f(n)\,e(g(n))$. We prove a quantitative dichotomy for the moments of $S_N$: for each integer $s\ge 2$, either $\mathbb{E}|S_N|^{2s}$ is close to the Gaussian moment $s!$, or the coefficients of $g$ can be approximated by rationals with a small denominator. In particular, if the coefficients of $g$ satisfy a Diophantine condition, then $S_N$ converges in law to a complex normal distribution with mean $0$ and variance $1$.
